terms.definition: A tiny infectious agent of genetic material in a protein coat - not a living cell.
terms.function: Infects host cells to make more copies of itself.
terms.whereItIs: In water, air, and in bodies, waiting to meet a host cell.
terms.whyItMatters: It causes many illnesses and is important to vaccines and infection.

terms.definition: The outer protein shell of a virus that holds supplies its genetic material.
terms.function: Protects the genes and helps the virus to get into a cell.
terms.whereItIs: The outer covering of the virus particle.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the structure that makes a virus a package, not a cell.

terms.definition: A living cell that a virus invades to use its machinery to reproduce.
terms.function: Provides the parts the virus lacks to make its copies.
terms.whereItIs: Any living cell the virus targets.
terms.whyItMatters: The host is required to reproduce - a virus cannot copy itself by itself.

terms.definition: The process in which a virus enters cells and forces them to make many new viruses.
terms.function: Virus spreads from cell to cell in the body.
terms.whereItIs: In the cells that the virus targets.
terms.whyItMatters: It is how a virus illness spreads through a whole body.
